newsitem.title: UK: Land up on continued institutional demand.
newsitem.headline: Land up on continued institutional demand.

text.p: Land Securities shares climbed to their highest level in almost three years amid continued institutional demand, dealers said.
But shares in other property concerns sank amid negative comments from at least two brokerages, dealers said.
By 1007 GMT, shares in Land Securities were up 7-1/2p to 771, having advances as high as 774-1/2 earlier.

The sector turned broadly mixed after UBS told its clients to take profits, dealers said. Shares in MEPC led the drop, stumbling 10p to 462, as Kleinwort Benson downgraded the stock to a "hold" from a "trading buy," they said.
Neither brokerage would comment on their recommendations.
One dealer said investors turned cautious on the sector after having had a good run.

"We've known for some time that demand for residential property is strong and it just spilled over into the commercial side. We've seen good demand across the board ... but I think they've gone up far enough," he added.
